target_profile.system_boundary: Captured OmniPaxos core, storage and optional async runtime. Caller owns message transport and application consumption; actor owns ticking, command serialization and append-notification completion.

activities.purpose: Qualified support for decision formation and legal advancement
activities.realization_summary: Prepare quorum selects accepted history; acceptance quorum advances decided prefix.

activities.purpose: Context validity and acquisition, transfer or loss of authority
activities.realization_summary: BLE proposes ballots; promise and role/phase checks qualify replication.

activities.purpose: Recovery and resynchronization of eligible participation
activities.realization_summary: Stored promises, reconnects and sequence gaps enter recovery; Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync restore participation.
Cluster validates quorum overlap and bounds; StopSign proposes a new cluster.
Public reads classify decided entries and compacted prefix summaries. Runtime subscriptions consume these vectors using per-subscriber counters and expose ordered streams.

activities.purpose: History, persistence and reconstruction of support
activities.realization_summary: Construction loads protocol metadata and reconstructs accepted extent; synchronization uses ordered storage transactions. MemoryStorage is volatile; PersistentStorage uses RocksDB batches.

activities.purpose: Client contracts, invocation intervals and observed completion
activities.realization_summary: Core callers deliver messages and tick; optional in-repository actor serializes commands, drives timers, tracks assignments and resolves append_notify using decided index and ballot.

implementation_guards: New leader ballot exceeds remembered leader and promise; follower accepts higher promise or equal promise in Recover.
writes: Flush pending batches; persist promise; reset leader support on local leadership; reset follower sequence on prepare.
external_effects: Queue Prepare or Promise containing accepted round, accepted index and decided index; selected history may include log sync.
important_branches: Construction with stored promise enters Recover and requests preparation. BLE initializes recovered leadership context separately and lowers own initial round to prevent same-ballot recovery leadership.

behaviors.protocol_context: Current leader ballot; Prepare then Accept
implementation_guards: Promise ballot equals leader ballot; distinct promise slots counted toward prepare quorum. Accepted requires current ballot and Leader/Accept.
writes: Choose maximal accepted round/index history; synchronize log; append buffered proposals unless stopped; record accepted indexes and update decided index when acceptance quorum supports it.
external_effects: Queue AcceptSync, AcceptDecide and Decide messages for promised followers.
unknowns: Same-ballot recovery may replace peer support metadata; accepted indexes are assigned rather than max-merged. Consequence depends on permitted message history.

implementation_guards: AcceptSync requires promised ballot and Follower/Prepare; incremental AcceptDecide requires Follower/Accept and expected sequence. Decide requires Accept phase and expected sequence.
writes: AcceptSync installs supplied history, decided index and sequence; incremental messages append entries and advance decided index with batching bounds.
external_effects: Queue or coalesce Accepted responses after accepted storage changes.
unknowns: AcceptSync does not check its sequence against a retained prior session; determine whether older same-ballot synchronization can reach a later Prepare phase under the actual transport contract.

behaviors.protocol_context: Reconnect, sequence gap or stored promise
writes: Reconnect to current leader sets Follower/Recover. PrepareReq clears leader promise slot and pending accept metadata before sending Prepare.
external_effects: Periodic resend sends cached Promise in Prepare or PrepareReq in Recover; leader retries prepares for unpromised peers.

cross_activity_effects.A2: Permits equal-ballot Prepare after entering Recover.
cross_activity_effects.A1: Resynchronization replaces follower history before ordinary acceptance resumes.

unknowns: Caller delivery ordering and whether old-connection messages may remain deliverable after reconnection.

implementation_guards: Heartbeat reply round and ballot configuration match; takeover requires unhappy neighbors and prepare quorum connectivity.
external_effects: Queue heartbeat requests and replies; invoke handle_leader when local ballot is selected.
unknowns: Heartbeat reply accumulation counts vector entries; participant uniqueness and duplicate-delivery assumptions need source investigation.

behaviors.protocol_context: Replica construction and synchronized log history
writes: Load promise, accepted round, decided index, compacted index and StopSign from supplied backend; reconstruct accepted index from log length plus compacted prefix and StopSign.
sync_log updates cache and submits ordered atomic operations; caller panics on storage error.

cross_activity_effects.A2: Recovered promise determines Recover phase and BLE recovered leader; a recovered BLE node does not retain same-ballot leadership.
cross_activity_effects.A1: Synchronized accepted round, suffix and decided prefix determine subsequent acknowledgments.

unknowns: Persistent backend crash durability and in-memory cache state after storage errors are not established by the read transaction API.

behaviors.protocol_context: Current accepted log and decided-index boundary
reads: Storage entries and current cached decided index.
external_effects: Entries below decided index become LogEntry::Decided; later accepted entries become Undecided; compaction has separate output variants.

cross_activity_effects.A7: Provides an independent public log-content observation for client completion checks.

behaviors.protocol_context: Pending EntryId and ballot-scoped assigned end index
behaviors.trigger: AppendNotify command dispatch, append_tracked, reconcile_unconfirmed and Assigned receipt
implementation_guards: Deferred batch tracking ignores entries whose stored ballot differs from current promise.
writes: Pending record gets a generated EntryId and deadline. record_assignment matches EntryId and stores (idx, ballot). Immediate local append records new accepted end index; deferred records are reconciled on ticks; remote Assigned messages also record assignments.
external_effects: Remote assignments are sent back to origin; pending append future remains outstanding.
important_branches: Incoming core synchronization does not clear already recorded Pending.assigned. It remains until a notifier outcome or actor shutdown.
unknowns: Remote and deferred-batch assignment lifecycles across authority changes remain separate.

behaviors.protocol_context: Pending assigned operations and current local decided prefix
behaviors.trigger: Actor tick after core tick, event emission, dispatch and reconciliation
reads: Pending assigned (idx,ballot), current promise, current decided index and deadline.
writes: Removes pending and resolves Ok(idx) when idx <= decided, before considering ballot supersession; otherwise returns Superseded for older ballot or Timeout after deadline.
external_effects: Resolve original append_notify oneshot to the caller.
important_branches: When synchronization replaces an unchosen assigned entry and advances decided extent before the next drain, the pending assignment remains and the numeric-success arm precedes supersession; the success predicate does not establish entry correspondence.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Consumes core decided-prefix advancement as success evidence.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Uses current promise to reject some superseded assignments, after the success arm.

existing_protections: A newer promise produces Superseded when assigned index remains beyond the decided prefix.
Quorum adoption may preserve an old entry across a ballot change; a changed ballot alone is not proof of a false success.

behaviors.protocol_context: Single actor serializes commands, incoming messages and timers
external_effects: Timer branches tick core and drain completion; egress periodically retrieves core messages. Incoming branch mutates core but does not drain notifiers immediately.
Bounded outgoing buffering preserves retained message order and can discard oldest traffic at capacity.
async_boundaries: Event emission is awaited during tick; network transport remains caller-owned.
Dropping all handles closes command/incoming senders; run exits on a closed input.

cross_activity_effects.A2: Incoming higher-ballot preparation can precede a later timer-driven completion drain.
cross_activity_effects.A1: Core may process multiple protocol messages and advance decisions between notifier drains.

behaviors.protocol_context: Decided log prefix in one replica
implementation_guards: Requested compacted index must not exceed decided boundary; only a larger compacted index writes state.
writes: Store trimmed prefix boundary and optional snapshot; retain suffix log entries.
external_effects: Local-only snapshot emits no peer compaction request; nonlocal success queues peer requests.

cross_activity_effects.A5: Reads before the compacted index return one summary marker followed by the retained suffix, rather than one element per original position.

implementation_guards: No read when cursor >= decided boundary. Full channel stops this push; closed channel removes subscription.
reads: Per-subscriber next_idx, minimum next_idx, decided extent and read_decided_suffix.
writes: Initial cursor is requested from index. Each successfully enqueued LogEntry increments cursor by one. Fanout indexes returned vector by sub.next_idx minus minimum cursor.
external_effects: Queue decided-log representations to each independent subscriber.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Consumes the prefix that consensus has marked decided for ordered application exposure.
cross_activity_effects.A7: Implements subscribe_decided stream-order contract and channel backpressure.

existing_protections: Individual subscriber cursors and try_send preserve order when each read vector element corresponds to one original log position.
unknowns: After one snapshot marker represents several positions, does count-based cursor advancement cause later emitted Decided entries to move backward in original log order?

facts.meaning: Replica has recorded the ballot to which its acceptance handling is currently promised.
facts.validity_context: Stored promise ballot; equal-ballot recovery can change phase and session without increasing it.
facts.durability: Promise is stored through Storage and loaded at construction. MemoryStorage is volatile; PersistentStorage stores it in RocksDB. Crash durability of backend settings remains a separate unknown.
facts.recovery: InternalStorage::load_cache reads the backend promise; SequencePaxos constructor enters Recover when get_promise returns Some and sends PrepareReq. BLE initializes from recovered promise with its own recovery round.
unknowns: Persistent backend crash durability under configured options.

facts.meaning: Pending client operation has a recorded assigned log end index and assignment ballot, associated by its EntryId.
facts.validity_context: Recorded assignment under its supplied ballot; this record alone does not establish that the same entry remains at the index after later synchronization.
facts.durability: Volatile actor state; removed on completion/error and lost at actor shutdown.
facts.recovery: No reconstruction of Pending records on actor restart is implemented in ActorState::new.
unknowns: Remote and deferred-batch assignment provenance under authority changes.

facts.meaning: Subscriber cursor equals its requested starting index plus the count of LogEntry values successfully enqueued for that subscriber.
facts.validity_context: From subscription creation until receiver closure/removal; the count includes compacted summary markers.
facts.recovery: No subscription reconstruction at actor restart; a new subscription starts at caller-provided from.
unknowns: Whether this count denotes the next original log position when read output contains a compacted prefix summary.

surfaces.reason: Does same-ballot recovery admit stale synchronization history after a later decision? Ballot/phase checks protect ordinary delivery; legal overlapping sessions and transport duties remain unresolved.
What ensures heartbeat support counts distinct eligible participants when replies are appended to a vector?
Does numeric decided-index success precede recognition that a different entry replaced this pending operation under a new ballot?
read_decided_suffix compresses a compacted prefix into one vector element, while fanout interprets vector offsets and successful-send counts as original log positions.

formation.explanation: Append is buffered during prepare, sent locally during Leader/Accept, or forwarded. Current-ballot promises populate participant slots; a prepare quorum selects maximal accepted-round/index history, synchronizes it, then sends AcceptSync. Followers synchronize and acknowledge, and incremental appends use sequence validation. Current-ballot Accepted messages update leader indexes; a write quorum causes decided-index advancement and decision propagation. Read APIs expose the decided prefix for application use. Storage load reconstructs accepted extent and reads classify entries against the decided boundary. The optional actor tracks a client EntryId to an assigned end index and ballot; on ticks it resolves success using decided index before testing ballot supersession. Ordered consumption also includes subscriptions: compacted-prefix reads contain a single summary marker, while runtime subscription cursors currently advance once per emitted representation.

context.explanation: Tick drives BLE; matching heartbeat rounds/configurations influence leader selection. SequencePaxos requires a higher ballot before initiating preparation. Followers persist a higher promise, reject lower-ballot replication and accept same-ballot prepare only during recovery. Reconnect and sequence gaps can initiate equal-ballot recovery. StopSign seals the old log and delegates startup/state transfer of a new configuration to the caller. Construction reads the stored promise into protocol and BLE recovery context, while cached accepted metadata comes from the backend. The actor serializes incoming messages and commands but runs completion processing only on tick branches.

connection.explanation: Authority alone does not enable acceptance: the new leader first gathers promise support and adopts accepted history, including prior decisions, before appending buffered work. A stopped selected history blocks appends. Followers require the promised ballot and appropriate phase; incremental old-session work is rejected or triggers recovery. Equal-ballot recovery resets phase and sequence before synchronization, leaving a specific delayed-AcceptSync history question. Client assignment records survive incoming higher-ballot synchronization until a later notifier drain. Whether the assigned entry survives depends on adopted history, rather than on numeric decided-index advancement alone. For the already read runtime consumer, stored assignment alone does not imply entry preservation: core synchronization can replace unchosen history while Pending.assigned stays unchanged, and the notifier numeric-success arm precedes supersession.

Actor event backpressure and compacted subscription cursor handling.

core_overview.rationale: Both core paths now connect initialization, storage reconstruction, quorum adoption, authority transitions, stale-message guards, retries, decided reads and actor completion. Local transport/session and backend-failure details remain open without blocking this backbone.
